facts: The Union of India and other appellant authorities have by these appeals challenged the findings recorded by the different Benches of the Tribunal in reply to one or the other' of or all the aforesaid three questions, in the decisions impugned therein.

The Government of India (Deptt. of Personnel & Training) issued an Office Memorandum No, 22011/1/79. Estt. (A) dated January 30, 1982 on the subject of promotion of officers in whose cases 'the sealed cover procedure' had been followed but against whom disciplinary/court proceedings were pending for a long time.

The Government, therefore, in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission examined how the hardship caused to the Government servant in such circumstances can be mitigated and has laid down the following procedure in such cases:

Para 4 of the Memorandum states that if the officer concerned is acquitted in the court proceedings on the merits of the case or exonerated in departmental disciplinary proceedings, the ad hoc promotion already made may be confirmed and the promotion treated as a regular one from the date of the ad hoc promotion with all attendant benefits.

To bring the record up-to-date, it may be pointed out that in view of the decision of this Court in Union of India & Anr. v. Tajinder Singh, [1986] 2 Scale 860 1986 Indlaw SC 507 decided on September 26, 1986, the Government of India in the Deptt. of Personnel & Training issued another' Office Memorandum No.
issues: What is the date from which it can be said that disciplinary/criminal proceedings are pending against an employee?
What is the course to be adopted when the employee is held guilty in such proceedings if the guilt merits punishment other than that of dismissal?
To what benefits an employee who is completely or partially exonerated is entitled to and from which date?'
Whether the sealed cover procedure is valid and whether it can be used to keep the findings of the DPC in a sealed cover until the disciplinary/court proceedings are over.

What is the procedure for ad hoc appointment of the concerned officer when the disciplinary/court proceedings are not concluded even after the expiry of two years from the date of the DPC which first considered him for promotion and whose findings are kept in the sealed cover, provided however that the officer is not under suspension.
court_reasoning: The Full Bench of the Tribunal has also struck down two provisions of the Central Government Memorandum of 30th January, 1982 on the subject.
This Court in Union of India & Anr. v. Tajinder Singh, [1986] 2 Scale 860 1986 Indlaw SC 507 decided on September 26, 1986

The existing instructions provide that in a case where departmental disciplinary proceedings have been held under the relevant disciplinary rules, 'warning' should not be issued as a result of such proceedings.
If it is found as a result of the proceedings that some blame attaches to the officer, then the penalty of censure at least should be imposed.
holding: The Union of India and other appellant authorities have by these appeals challenged the findings recorded by the different Benches of the Tribunal in reply to one or the other' of or all the aforesaid three questions, in the decisions impugned therein.
